pages.text: Aging needs $(item)Warmth 0 or lower$(), environmental $(item)Humidity 1–3$(), and $(thing)cool/dark storage$(): the block above the barrel must not see the sky and block light above the barrel must be 7 or less.

Every $(item)24,000 ticks$() of uninterrupted aging conditions counts as 1 aged day. The tooltip labels are: under 7 days Fresh, under 30 Light Aged, under 90 Deep Aged, under 365 Vintage, and 365+ Cellared.
pages.title: Aging Time

pages.text: Quality gains slow over time:$(br2)Days 1–7: +1 every 3 days$(br)Days 8–30: +1 every 7 days$(br)Days 31–90: +1 every 15 days$(br)Days 91–365: +1 every 30 days$(br2)Quality can rise as high as 120.
pages.title: Quality Schedule

pages.text: After day 365 there are no further aging-quality gains. The barrel begins periodic spoil checks instead. The chance grows with extreme age, up to a 10% monthly check. Very old tobacco is therefore a prestige/risk choice, not free infinite quality.
pages.title: Extreme Age
